issues.legal_issue: The bar on suits by unregistered partnership firms against third parties does not extend to a suit concerning a transaction outside the firm’s business that seeks non-contractual or statutory relief.
material_facts: The plaintiff was an unregistered partnership firm engaged in building construction.
The challenged sale of the firm’s share in property was an independent transaction, not one entered into in the course of the firm’s building business.
The suit alleged fraud and misrepresentation in obtaining the sale deed and sought to have it declared void and to obtain an injunction.
The defendants sought rejection of the plaint on the ground that the firm was unregistered.
The courts below found that the sale transaction did not arise from the plaintiff firm’s business; the Supreme Court did not decide the merits of the fraud allegations.
issues.conclusion: The bar under Section 69(2) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, did not apply to the suit. The High Court’s order rejecting the plaint was set aside, and the Trial Court’s order refusing rejection was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 69(2) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, the bar applies when the right sought to be enforced arises from a contract entered into by the plaintiff firm with the third-party defendant in the course of the firm’s business dealings with that defendant. It does not apply merely because a contract is mentioned as a historical fact or as the source of title to an asset, and it does not bar a suit enforcing a statutory or common-law right. The Court applied Raptakos Brett & Co. Ltd. v. Ganesh Property (1998) 7 SCC 184, as explained in Haldiram Bhujiawala v. Anand Kumar Deepak Kumar (2000) 3 SCC 250 and Purushottam v. Shivraj Fine Art Litho Works (2007) 15 SCC 58. The Court also addressed the application to reject the plaint under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

predicates.unregistered_firm_suit_against_third_par: An unregistered partnership firm brought a suit against a third party.
predicates.plaint_rejection_sought: The defendant sought rejection of the plaint as barred by law because the firm was unregistered.
predicates.transaction_outside_firm_business: The transaction challenged in the suit was independent of, and was not entered into in the course of, the firm’s business dealings.
predicates.claim_seeks_noncontractual_or_statutory_: The firm sought relief based on allegations of fraud or misrepresentation or on statutory or common-law rights, rather than enforcement of a right arising from a contract made with the defendant in the course of the firm’s business.

issues.definition: When an unregistered firm sues a third party, the defendant seeks rejection of the plaint, the challenged transaction is outside the firm’s business, and the firm seeks non-contractual or statutory relief, the suit is not barred by non-registration.
